proposal: The Mandate recommends dismantling USAID's DEI offices, advisers, dashboards and award requirements and considering debarment of partners that promote discriminatory DEI practices. It also recommends rescinding the Climate Strategy 2022 to 2030 and Paris Agreement-related programs, renaming the gender office as an office for women, children and families, rescinding the 2022 Gender Policy, and removing gender-related terms from agency materials, contracts and grants.

status_summary: USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department on 2025-07-01, as reported by NPR on that date and reflected in a Lead Inspector General report that records USAID programs moving to State management that day; the USAID-internal DEI, climate and gender steps the Mandate lists were not separately verified. Two State Department final rules published 2026-01-27 and effective 2026-02-26 add foreign assistance award terms: Combating Gender Ideology in Foreign Assistance (91 FR 3332, 2 CFR part 603) and Combating Discriminatory Equity Ideology in Foreign Assistance Rules (91 FR 3345, 2 CFR part 604). They apply to new awards and to existing awards that add funds; they bind foreign NGOs and international organizations, impose narrower terms on US NGOs and optional terms on foreign governments, require flow-down to subrecipients, define sex as a binary biological classification, and provide for termination, refund, suspension and debarment, with a national security or foreign policy waiver. Contract clauses await a separate rulemaking and the information collection awaits OMB approval. The 2026-01-07 withdrawal memorandum also lists the UNFCCC, IPCC and UN Women, and State's April 2025 reorganization plan was reported as expected to cut the Office of Global Women's Issues and DEI efforts. The rules cover all recipients of State foreign assistance, which is broader than the Mandate's focus on USAID's own apparatus and partners.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14151, Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programs and Preferencing, was issued; it was published in the Federal Register on 2025-01-29 as document 2025-01953 and is one of the orders both State rules list as consistent policy.
AP reported that State's reorganization was expected to cut the Office of Global Women's Issues and diversity and inclusion efforts.

USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department; the Lead Inspector General later reported that State took over management of remaining USAID programs that day, including five active Iraq programs and 15 humanitarian assistance programs covered by the report.
The Rescissions Act of 2025 rescinded $125 million from the Clean Technology Fund account among other foreign assistance accounts.
The withdrawal memorandum directed exit from bodies including the UNFCCC, the IPCC and UN Women (published 2026-01-16).

State published final rules adding 2 CFR parts 603 (gender ideology) and 604 (discriminatory equity ideology) with award terms for foreign assistance recipients, issued without notice and comment under grants and foreign-affairs exemptions; the gender rule lists Executive Orders 14151 and 14168, and the equity rule lists Executive Orders 14151 and 14173, as consistent policies.

GAO reported under the Congressional Review Act that State's Combating Gender Ideology in Foreign Assistance rule is a major rule (State estimated $16.0 million in one-time and $114.1 million in annual compliance costs); GAO does not rule on the rule's compliance.
Both rules took effect for new awards and for existing awards that add funds; contracts are not yet covered and a separate rulemaking is planned.

title: End DEI, climate and gender programming in foreign assistance
uncertainties: The USAID-internal steps the Mandate lists (Chief Diversity Officer, Climate Strategy rescission, renaming of the gender office) were not found in any document read and are treated as overtaken by agency changes rather than verified; the closure of USAID rests on an NPR report of 2025-07-01 and a Lead Inspector General report (released 2026-02-20, read on the USAID OIG site) that confirms USAID programs moved to State management on 2025-07-01 and an ongoing operational drawdown but does not describe the agency's closure as a whole. The equity rule (2 CFR part 604) was read in full in review; the gender rule (2 CFR part 603) was read through its first 100,000 characters, which include the operative terms, and its closing appendix text and footnotes were not read. Executive Orders 14168 and 14173 are confirmed only as listed in the text of the rules; only 14151 was checked as a Federal Register document. Litigation over the rules and any OMB approval or contract rulemaking after 2026-02-26 were not exhaustively researched; no court challenge was found.
